::: {#exm-marginal-likelihood-uniform}
#### Posterior for a coin's probability of heads under a uniform prior

As in @exm-posterior,
let $\param$ be a coin's probability of heads,
now allowed to take any value in $(0, 1)$,
with the uniform prior density $\p(\param) = 1$ for $\param \in (0, 1)$.
One toss lands heads;
call that observation $y = 1$,
so $\p(y = 1 \mid \param) = \param$.
The [marginal likelihood](#def-marginal-likelihood) is an integral over $\param$:

$$
\ba
\p(y = 1)
&= \int_0^1 \p(y = 1 \mid \param)\, \p(\param)\, d\param
&& \text{(definition of the marginal likelihood)}\\
&= \int_0^1 \param \cdot 1\, d\param
&& \text{(substituting the likelihood and the prior)}\\
&= \int_0^1 \param\, d\param
&& \text{($\param \cdot 1 = \param$)}\\
&= \sb{\frac{\param^2}{2}}_0^1
&& \text{(antiderivative of $\param$)}\\
&= \frac{1^2}{2} - \frac{0^2}{2}
&& \text{(evaluating at the limits)}\\
&= \frac{1}{2}
&& \text{(arithmetic)}.
\ea
$$

By @thm-bayes-posterior,
for $\param \in (0, 1)$:

$$
\ba
\p(\param \mid y = 1)
&= \frac{\p(y = 1 \mid \param)\, \p(\param)}{\p(y = 1)}
&& \text{(Bayes' theorem for parameters)}\\
&= \frac{\param \cdot 1}{1/2}
&& \text{(substituting the likelihood, prior, and marginal likelihood)}\\
&= \frac{\param}{1/2}
&& \text{($\param \cdot 1 = \param$)}\\
&= 2\param
&& \text{(dividing by $1/2$ is multiplying by 2)}.
\ea
$$

One head moves the posterior density toward large values of $\param$.
The posterior mean is

$$
\ba
\E{\param \mid y = 1}
&= \int_0^1 \param \cdot \p(\param \mid y = 1)\, d\param
&& \text{(expectation under the posterior density)}\\
&= \int_0^1 \param \cdot 2\param\, d\param
&& \text{(substituting the posterior density)}\\
&= \int_0^1 2\param^2\, d\param
&& \text{($\param \cdot \param = \param^2$)}\\
&= \sb{\frac{2\param^3}{3}}_0^1
&& \text{(antiderivative of $2\param^2$)}\\
&= \frac{2 \cdot 1^3}{3} - \frac{2 \cdot 0^3}{3}
&& \text{(evaluating at the limits)}\\
&= \frac{2}{3}
&& \text{(arithmetic)},
\ea
$$

up from the prior mean of $1/2$.
:::
